(i) task-global differential privacy is a more practical privacy guarantee for meta-learning than local differential privacy, and (ii) a new differentially-private algorithm for meta-learning that satisfies task-global differential privacy also satisfies standard transfer-learning guarantees.

we propose the first differentially private algorithm with provable guarantees for meta-learning, and that we empirically demonstrate the benefit of relaxing the privacy guarantee from local privacy to task-global privacy.

(a) we introduce task-global differential privacy, a more realistic privacy notion than local or global differential privacy in the meta-learning setting, and (b) we propose the first algorithm that achieves task-global differential privacy in gradient-based meta-learning.

we provide a new algorithm for parameter transfer that is private and also provably achieves good performance in convex settings.

we introduce a new privacy notion called task-global differential privacy and propose a new algorithm for parameter-transfer meta-learning that provably satisfies this privacy requirement in convex settings.

we propose a new differentiable private algorithm for gradient based parameter transfer that not just satisfies this privacy requirement however also keeps provable transfer learning assurances in convex settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the privacy guarantees of a meta-learning algorithm should be tailored to the threat model of interest.
, when privacy is considered, the choice of privacy model can have a large impact on the utility of learning algorithms.
privacy is not an obstacle for meta-learning and can be used to improve its performance in many applications.
